observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with white walls, a ceiling-mounted air-conditioner on the upper left, a row of track lights on the dark ceiling, and a full-height mirror wall on the right. A woman with a dark ponytail, neon-yellow tank top, white flared skirt, neon-yellow leg warmers and white sneakers performs in the center, seen mostly from behind, while her front-facing mirror image appears on the right. The camera viewpoint and background fixtures stay fixed across the excerpt.
visible_changes: The woman's right arm lifts from a low side position, rises through a bent phase near the head, and reaches a near-vertical overhead extension (frames ~1-13), then bends back down toward the head (frames ~14-17).
Both arms then come up flexed in front of the chest/face (frames ~17-21) before lowering to the sides (frames ~22-25).
Her torso rotates continuously from a back-facing stance to a right-side profile stance (frames ~17-24); this is body rotation, not a camera move or a cut.

From the side profile, the right arm extends toward the mirror, then raises again with the index finger pointing up, holding the raised position (frames ~26-37), and finally bends down with both arms flexed in front of the chest (frames ~38-41).
Her weight shifts and feet reposition slightly throughout (e.g., one heel lifting around frames 5-9 and the stance narrowing during the turn), with the skirt swaying accordingly.
The mirror reflection reproduces these same arm and torso changes as a mirrored image, confirming the moving entity is one person and the right-side figure is her reflection, not a second dancer.
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreography before t=0 and after t=1.60, including whether the raised-arm gestures are repeated or lead into a different step, is not shown.
The musical or instructional context prompting each movement is unseen.
uncertain_details: Whether the body turn is a deliberate step or a balance shift cannot be determined from pose alone.
The exact hand shape (open palm vs. pointing finger) at several mid-frames is partly blurred by motion.
